Liver enzyme labs—commonly part of a liver panel or comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP)—`measure blood levels of enzymes and other substances to check for liver injury, bile duct issues, or overall liver health`.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1-b3D5UlKZf_Sv0n0nvQNzMuzEGmA2FbhzcZctAHPRNJtpMfuXPLiMeiFAu7Q1wQ1_aCLGNJADFO91VrWz1UBc0YM1K7-6roIkm9lVhFeZV6scufgvOhU6pXQQYwNObEpBTIY1MnH0zb5mcTkRTB9NDFCIEGfV9YvGih4lJxcBIxlcDh4sBZIf05dCU)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXqO6ikY2oyenvjieDYBrYfSr9Jkiux-gkjktgLwGlD0jF7vUxsoP7F2gq9W_4T78Ox0-hzaTH2BfCm7ieoJNaLJlngda8OECPh3e4_NYp_0tTeXYMN28aYW8jE3l6t7SSHr3GwbOXteyXTpus_sfb)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHEIkXXXEwz31b_sD3p4lI-xJ-fnDVrDdPifUNnYKpmtsWuY8rZj1N2Aq2tzfKVuUeNsltvPmBpSDhcBPgbci9j65atFN9ZjSxPCTuGIPUq_MF8nyFQ8i63o3yXZNpD-ymlmKzXUNc)

### Key Liver Enzymes

- **ALT (Alanine transaminase):** Found mostly in the liver. High levels often point to liver cell injury.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF13fnRZHCnPlW4805JZV4MC3agRnNwC_ddK7Crs-0m9FDFdXg7T4pyJQEjN8LSE9xm0bgptMyNUkejK1nVnlfXBrEngdkhwWywzo_pW3BN3leUMw5TH1j6YfOnKfjq7yEvxlutbw_oOe1eIQBBYvngrLz1LewnF-nnutUy74Yf-CgEEdq2g)[[2]](https://liverfoundation.org/resource-center/videos/understanding-your-liver-function-test-results/)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHEIkXXXEwz31b_sD3p4lI-xJ-fnDVrDdPifUNnYKpmtsWuY8rZj1N2Aq2tzfKVuUeNsltvPmBpSDhcBPgbci9j65atFN9ZjSxPCTuGIPUq_MF8nyFQ8i63o3yXZNpD-ymlmKzXUNc)
- **AST (Aspartate aminotransferase):** Found in the liver as well as muscle, heart, and other tissues. High levels can signal liver or muscle stress.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1-b3D5UlKZf_Sv0n0nvQNzMuzEGmA2FbhzcZctAHPRNJtpMfuXPLiMeiFAu7Q1wQ1_aCLGNJADFO91VrWz1UBc0YM1K7-6roIkm9lVhFeZV6scufgvOhU6pXQQYwNObEpBTIY1MnH0zb5mcTkRTB9NDFCIEGfV9YvGih4lJxcBIxlcDh4sBZIf05dCU)[[2]](https://liverfoundation.org/resource-center/videos/understanding-your-liver-function-test-results/)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHEIkXXXEwz31b_sD3p4lI-xJ-fnDVrDdPifUNnYKpmtsWuY8rZj1N2Aq2tzfKVuUeNsltvPmBpSDhcBPgbci9j65atFN9ZjSxPCTuGIPUq_MF8nyFQ8i63o3yXZNpD-ymlmKzXUNc)
- **ALP (Alkaline phosphatase):** Found in the liver, bile ducts, and bones. Elevated levels may point to bile flow issues or bone conditions.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1-b3D5UlKZf_Sv0n0nvQNzMuzEGmA2FbhzcZctAHPRNJtpMfuXPLiMeiFAu7Q1wQ1_aCLGNJADFO91VrWz1UBc0YM1K7-6roIkm9lVhFeZV6scufgvOhU6pXQQYwNObEpBTIY1MnH0zb5mcTkRTB9NDFCIEGfV9YvGih4lJxcBIxlcDh4sBZIf05dCU)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESngEBxCJF11eD96HNZeZX9jv48WYbuIPZEOxlHeP-vNr6tu3xZ7_7HbP_Dc3QlOMrb8IBrOw0Zhnenaxs20ufgPyAu7Kprczm8j8x6w5AUhef8XymwsR8U9SCejVDrlgB2PypIolG3X7yY579V8PTbSl5hqE5xFR3qhQZmHicIOdsFKng2hijWjhlZgByxrmVkgSS1FcBeYKbt7AFgTmeOQ)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHEIkXXXEwz31b_sD3p4lI-xJ-fnDVrDdPifUNnYKpmtsWuY8rZj1N2Aq2tzfKVuUeNsltvPmBpSDhcBPgbci9j65atFN9ZjSxPCTuGIPUq_MF8nyFQ8i63o3yXZNpD-ymlmKzXUNc)[[4]](https://liverfoundation.org/resource-center/videos/understanding-your-liver-function-test-results/)
- **GGT (Gamma-glutamyl transferase):** Found in the liver and bile ducts. Often checked alongside ALP to help confirm a liver or bile duct source, or to evaluate alcohol or medication effects.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHEIkXXXEwz31b_sD3p4lI-xJ-fnDVrDdPifUNnYKpmtsWuY8rZj1N2Aq2tzfKVuUeNsltvPmBpSDhcBPgbci9j65atFN9ZjSxPCTuGIPUq_MF8nyFQ8i63o3yXZNpD-ymlmKzXUNc)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESngEBxCJF11eD96HNZeZX9jv48WYbuIPZEOxlHeP-vNr6tu3xZ7_7HbP_Dc3QlOMrb8IBrOw0Zhnenaxs20ufgPyAu7Kprczm8j8x6w5AUhef8XymwsR8U9SCejVDrlgB2PypIolG3X7yY579V8PTbSl5hqE5xFR3qhQZmHicIOdsFKng2hijWjhlZgByxrmVkgSS1FcBeYKbt7AFgTmeOQ)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHEIkXX5_WmO0rtZoCSVcm6R5xmZfCDLcTW5FM0SxDYYHCdOlufSD1XYXrT4BcK0QE5rm_0-VN3MkMXNLHBMDBUsVnQfrLGDZhPJ9AK2d_WYo8NymYEaPca9162ZJSwQFb6Kse43RuTj9LgqJ9aEfelXok-aw)

### Related Panel Markers
Panels often include non-enzyme markers such as **bilirubin** (a waste product processed by the liver), **albumin** and **total protein** , and **prothrombin time (PT)** to help assess how well the liver is functioning.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXqO6ikY2oyenvjieDYBrYfSr9Jkiux-gkjktgLwGlD0jF7vUxsoP7F2gq9W_4T78Ox0-hzaTH2BfCm7ieoJNaLJlngda8OECPh3e4_NYp_0tTeXYMN28aYW8jE3l6t7SSHr3GwbOXteyXTpus_sfb)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1-b3D5UlKZf_Sv0n0nvQNzMuzEGmA2FbhzcZctAHPRNJtpMfuXPLiMeiFAu7Q1wQ1_aCLGNJADFO91VrWz1UBc0YM1K7-6roIkm9lVhFeZV6scufgvOhU6pXQQYwNObEpBTIY1MnH0zb5mcTkRTB9NDFCIEGfV9YvGih4lJxcBIxlcDh4sBZIf05dCU)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHEIkXX5_WmO0rtZoCSVcm6R5xmZfCDLcTW5FM0SxDYYHCdOlufSD1XYXrT4BcK0QE5rm_0-VN3MkMXNLHBMDBUsVnQfrLGDZhPJ9AK2d_WYo8NymYEaPca9162ZJSwQFb6Kse43RuTj9LgqJ9aEfelXok-aw)

### Interpreting Results

- **Reference ranges vary:** Normal ranges depend on the specific lab, age, and sex, so compare results against the range listed on your report.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1-b3D5UlKZf_Sv0n0nvQNzMuzEGmA2FbhzcZctAHPRNJtpMfuXPLiMeiFAu7Q1wQ1_aCLGNJADFO91VrWz1UBc0YM1K7-6roIkm9lVhFeZV6scufgvOhU6pXQQYwNObEpBTIY1MnH0zb5mcTkRTB9NDFCIEGfV9YvGih4lJxcBIxlcDh4sBZIf05dCU)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHEIkXXXEwz31b_sD3p4lI-xJ-fnDVrDdPifUNnYKpmtsWuY8rZj1N2Aq2tzfKVuUeNsltvPmBpSDhcBPgbci9j65atFN9ZjSxPCTuGIPUq_MF8nyFQ8i63o3yXZNpD-ymlmKzXUNc)
- **Temporary vs. ongoing causes:** Mildly elevated enzymes can sometimes be temporary—linked to intense exercise, recent illness, or certain medications or supplements—while persistent elevations may point to conditions like fatty liver disease (MASLD), viral hepatitis, alcohol-related liver stress, or bile duct issues.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHEIkXXXEwz31b_sD3p4lI-xJ-fnDVrDdPifUNnYKpmtsWuY8rZj1N2Aq2tzfKVuUeNsltvPmBpSDhcBPgbci9j65atFN9ZjSxPCTuGIPUq_MF8nyFQ8i63o3yXZNpD-ymlmKzXUNc)
- **Next steps:** Abnormal labs alone rarely give a final diagnosis. A healthcare provider reviews the pattern of results alongside your history, medications, and symptoms, and may recommend repeat testing, imaging, or targeted blood work.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1-b3D5UlKZf_Sv0n0nvQNzMuzEGmA2FbhzcZctAHPRNJtpMfuXPLiMeiFAu7Q1wQ1_aCLGNJADFO91VrWz1UBc0YM1K7-6roIkm9lVhFeZV6scufgvOhU6pXQQYwNObEpBTIY1MnH0zb5mcTkRTB9NDFCIEGfV9YvGih4lJxcBIxlcDh4sBZIf05dCU)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXqO6ikY2oyenvjieDYBrYfSr9Jkiux-gkjktgLwGlD0jF7vUxsoP7F2gq9W_4T78Ox0-hzaTH2BfCm7ieoJNaLJlngda8OECPh3e4_NYp_0tTeXYMN28aYW8jE3l6t7SSHr3GwbOXteyXTpus_sfb)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF13fnRZHCnPlW4805JZV4MC3agRnNwC_ddK7Crs-0m9FDFdXg7T4pyJQEjN8LSE9xm0bgptMyNUkejK1nVnlfXBrEngdkhwWywzo_pW3BN3leUMw5TH1j6YfOnKfjq7yEvxlutbw_oOe1eIQBBYvngrLz1LewnF-nnutUy74Yf-CgEEdq2g)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHEIkXXXEwz31b_sD3p4lI-xJ-fnDVrDdPifUNnYKpmtsWuY8rZj1N2Aq2tzfKVuUeNsltvPmBpSDhcBPgbci9j65atFN9ZjSxPCTuGIPUq_MF8nyFQ8i63o3yXZNpD-ymlmKzXUNc)

For more details on what these tests measure and how results are used, see the [Mayo Clinic](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1-b3D5UlKZf_Sv0n0nvQNzMuzEGmA2FbhzcZctAHPRNJtpMfuXPLiMeiFAu7Q1wQ1_aCLGNJADFO91VrWz1UBc0YM1K7-6roIkm9lVhFeZV6scufgvOhU6pXQQYwNObEpBTIY1MnH0zb5mcTkRTB9NDFCIEGfV9YvGih4lJxcBIxlcDh4sBZIf05dCU) and [MedlinePlus](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXqO6ikY2oyenvjieDYBrYfSr9Jkiux-gkjktgLwGlD0jF7vUxsoP7F2gq9W_4T78Ox0-hzaTH2BfCm7ieoJNaLJlngda8OECPh3e4_NYp_0tTeXYMN28aYW8jE3l6t7SSHr3GwbOXteyXTpus_sfb).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1-b3D5UlKZf_Sv0n0nvQNzMuzEGmA2FbhzcZctAHPRNJtpMfuXPLiMeiFAu7Q1wQ1_aCLGNJADFO91VrWz1UBc0YM1K7-6roIkm9lVhFeZV6scufgvOhU6pXQQYwNObEpBTIY1MnH0zb5mcTkRTB9NDFCIEGfV9YvGih4lJxcBIxlcDh4sBZIf05dCU)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXqO6ikY2oyenvjieDYBrYfSr9Jkiux-gkjktgLwGlD0jF7vUxsoP7F2gq9W_4T78Ox0-hzaTH2BfCm7ieoJNaLJlngda8OECPh3e4_NYp_0tTeXYMN28aYW8jE3l6t7SSHr3GwbOXteyXTpus_sfb)If you'd like to narrow this down, share a bit more context:

items.text: Reference ranges vary: Normal ranges depend on the specific lab, age, and sex, so compare results against the range listed on your report. Temporary vs. ongoing causes: Mildly elevated enzymes can sometimes be temporary—linked to intense exercise, recent illness, or certain medications or supplements—while persistent elevations may point to conditions like fatty liver disease (MASLD), viral hepatitis, alcohol-related liver stress, or bile duct issues. Next steps: Abnormal labs alone rarely give a final diagnosis. A healthcare provider reviews the pattern of results alongside your history, medications, and symptoms, and may recommend repeat testing, imaging, or targeted blood work.
